# HTTP contract

The exact route registry is authoritative:

- `internal/transport/http/admin/v1/router.go` — administrative content management.
- `internal/transport/http/api/v1/router.go` — public and audience-aware read APIs.
- `internal/transport/http/private/router.go` — service-to-service reads.
- `internal/transport/http/router.go` — mounts and middleware.

Administrative routes are mounted both without a prefix and under `/admin/v1`; the unprefixed surface is a compatibility contract. Public routes are under `/api/v1`. Internal routes are under `/internal` only when an internal token is configured.

## Authorization

`TEACHER`, `ADMIN`, and `MODERATOR` may read administrative content. Only `ADMIN` and `MODERATOR` may mutate content, hierarchy, tasks, starter files, or apply a knowledge-import batch.

Public routes accept guests. A trusted `X-User-Role` is attached as the audience for lesson policy. Privileged administrative roles bypass lesson read restrictions; other audiences follow `GUEST`, `STUDENT`, `STUDENT_PRO`, or disabled access. See [Lesson read access](lesson-read-access.md).
Public task projections redact assessment answer keys, including
`expected_answers` nested in a text-quiz `code_structure`. Trusted evaluation
consumers obtain the complete contract only from the internal task endpoint.

General internal callers provide `X-Internal-Token` matching `INTERNAL_API_TOKEN`.
The generated Course write accepts only the distinct
`LEARNING_PLANNER_INTERNAL_TOKEN`; diagnostic assessment discovery is a
separately rollout-gated read and accepts only
`DIAGNOSTIC_CATALOG_INTERNAL_TOKEN`. Each configured token must be distinct.
Token comparison is a service shared-secret boundary, not end-user
authorization.

`POST /internal/generated-courses` is the atomic Course ensure command owned by
the Learning Planner integration. It requires the dedicated token and a UUID
`Idempotency-Key`, accepts
one fully generated normalized `ACTIVE` Course with `catalog_visible=false`
and `ACTIVE` Lessons, and returns `course_id`, `reused`, and ordered lesson
bindings with their authoritative targets. The command locks the idempotency
key and `CourseFingerprint`, creates the ordinary Course hierarchy, localized
lesson descriptions, examples, `quiz_theory` knowledge checks, target
references, and planning provenance in one transaction, and reuses an exact
existing fingerprint. Incomplete/planned content is rejected, so a partially
generated course never becomes readable. Reusing one idempotency key with a
different normalized body returns `409`.

`GET /internal/course/get-internal-diagnostic-assessments/{courseID}` is a
Learning Planner diagnostic-catalog read and requires the distinct
`DIAGNOSTIC_CATALOG_INTERNAL_TOKEN`, not the general or Planner write token.
When the read token is empty, the route is disabled. The catalog contains only
active diagnostic assessment tasks of types `11`, `12`, or `13` with exact
uppercase `evaluation_mode=AUTO`; an explicit diagnostic task with another or
invalid mode fails the read with a validation error.

The complete serialized generated Course document is limited to 16 MiB. The
same limit is enforced by the transport and generated-Course use case, matching
the Learning Planner producer contract. Human-readable title limits count
Unicode characters rather than UTF-8 bytes.

The same command supports Learning Planner's lazy practice materialization.
For that flow the request contains one complete active Lesson under the normal
Course hierarchy and uses fingerprint version
`practice-material-fingerprint-v1`. Calls occur only when a student opens a
missing route material. The target/policy/locale fingerprint enables reuse
across compatible task instances; Course never stores the frozen route itself.

`POST /internal/course/resolve-lesson-bindings` accepts up to 1,000 exact
`course_source_key` / `lesson_source_key` pairs and returns the live UUID pair
only when the lesson is actually placed in that course. It is a read-only
cross-service identity boundary: callers must not derive IDs from source keys.
Unresolved pairs are returned in `missing` so an importer can fail its own
preflight before writing another service.

`GET /internal/lesson/{lessonID}/teacher-context?language=<code>` returns only
an active lesson's current Course-owned content snapshot. The response contains
`lesson_id`, optional `course_id`/`section_id`, resolved `language`, `title`,
`excerpt`, `description`, and `content_revision`; the revision is the lesson's
UTC `updated_at` formatted as RFC3339Nano. An exact requested translation is
used when present, otherwise the base lesson fields are returned with language
`default`. Text is UTF-8 and bounded; a missing or inactive lesson returns 404.
The endpoint exposes current state only and provides no historical lookup. It
is intended for a trusted Teacher verifier; consumers must not send the whole
snapshot to a model when only a student-selected fragment is needed.

## Change rules

- Update router tests and this contract when a mount, authorization rule, error shape, or route changes.
- Treat removal of legacy unprefixed admin routes as a coordinated breaking change.
- Verify public visibility through the full hierarchy; do not authorize a reusable lesson through an unrelated, more permissive course placement.
- Keep `README.md` endpoint examples synchronized, but derive exact paths and parameters from route source files.

## Immutable lesson assignments (cutover)

`POST /internal/lessons/{lessonID}/revision` resolves the current active lesson
into an immutable definition; no body is required. `GET
/internal/lesson-revisions/{revisionID}` retrieves that exact persisted
revision. Both require `X-Internal-Token`. Invalid identities/policies return
422; missing/inactive lessons return 404. Definitions use
`schema=lesson-revision.v1`, `lesson_id`, `lesson_revision_id`, `content`, and
`activities`. Each activity has a stable UUID `activity_id`, `type`, `required`,
and `source_reference: {id, revision_id}`. Types are `theory_acknowledged`,
`quiz_passed`, `task_passed`, and `practice_completed`. Task/quiz references bind
to the containing LessonRevision; practice references bind to an explicit
PracticeRevision (`id` and `revision_id` both identify that exact revision). Content includes lesson text/localizations/examples and
snapshotted task definitions. `content.tasks` uses the existing trusted
internal Task JSON, including assessment answer keys. Student must omit answer
keys when presenting learner content; these endpoints are never public.

`PUT /admin/v1/lesson/{lessonID}/completion-policy` accepts
`{"activities":[...]}` under the existing ADMIN/MODERATOR write authorization.
It authors future snapshots only. Duplicate activity IDs, unknown types,
missing practice revision UUIDs, foreign/inactive task references, and policies
without any required activity are rejected. Optional activities do not block
Student completion. Without an authored policy, each active task becomes a
required passed activity; a taskless lesson requires explicit theory
acknowledgement. Course never records learner satisfaction or item completion.

Generated-Course receipts add `lessons[].lesson_revision_id`; Planner must carry
that exact identity into Student assignment. Historical legacy assignments are
not backfilled with current revisions. They retain legacy semantics until
explicit reassignment. The old `/internal/course-progress/lessons` endpoint
remains a legacy projection and cannot authorize new item completion.

The explicit runtime fixture `test/runtime/lesson_completion_fixture.sql` is
for a newly migrated disposable database only. It supplies a lesson and one
single-choice assessment for Student's `test/runtime/lesson_completion_smoke.py`
proof. The proof assigns R10 twice, publishes R11, changes the current answer
key, and verifies that official attempts still score against the assigned R10.
Practice's opt-in `TestPracticeCompletionReachesAssignedStudentRequirement`
then drives the real Runtime and Student owners; its unrelated Catalog,
Planner, Sandbox, and Validator dependencies are test doubles.

## T23 starter upload routing proof

The existing canonical admin upload is
`POST /admin/v1/task/{taskID}/starter-files/upload`, using multipart `files`
and corresponding relative `paths`. Course's existing `ADMIN`/`MODERATOR`
write allowlist trusts the Gateway's `X-User-ID` and `X-User-Role` metadata.
This proof changes no production route, authorization or archive policy.

Root may launch `TestT23ServeStarterUploadProvider` with the `integration`
build tag and `T23_COURSE_PROVIDER=1`. It requires the exact URL
`postgres://postgres@127.0.0.1:58998/remediation_t23_course_integration_proof?sslmode=disable`.
Root creates and migrates this isolated database before launch; the provider
performs no DDL, retains all seeded rows, and stops on its marker or after a
finite 20 minute lifetime. It composes the production admin router, task
handler, upload use case, PostgreSQL repositories and transaction manager,
and FileStorage HTTP client. Two fresh bounded CODE task metadata fixtures
separate the canonical preflight from the frontend proof. Their code is
never executed.

Set `T23_COURSE_DATABASE_URL`, `T23_COURSE_PROVIDER_INFO_FILE`,
`T23_COURSE_PROVIDER_STOP_FILE`, and `T23_COURSE_PROVIDER_EVENTS_FILE`.
The three fresh evidence paths must reside inside the remediation report's
`EVIDENCE/T23` directory. Root supplies distinct ephemeral `T23_ADMIN_TOKEN`,
`T23_MODERATOR_TOKEN`, `T23_STUDENT_TOKEN`, `T23_TEACHER_TOKEN`, and
`T23_PROOF_TOKEN` in process environment only. Optional `T23_BAD_TOKEN`
must remain unauthorized. No tokens appear in readiness, request journals,
or readback.

Readiness schema `t23-starter-provider.v1` contains separate `course_origin`
and `auth_origin` with their ports, `database`, `task_id`, `preflight_task_id`,
`readback_url`, and evidence paths. Gateway renders an empty `AUTH_BASE_PATH`
and sends its production `POST /auth/verify` JSON `{token}` to the named
Auth collaborator. That collaborator returns `{user_id, claims:{role}}`
only for a supplied actor token and returns 401 for missing or invalid tokens.
The named FileStorage collaborator consumes the actual production client's
bounded ZIP upload and activation calls, keeps ZIP bytes in memory, and
records their hashes and entry names. These collaborators do not prove live
Auth JWT validation, FileStorage/MinIO persistence or educational authoring.

`GET /__t23/state?task_id=<owned task>` requires `X-Proof-Token` and returns
actual PostgreSQL `bindings`, `binding_count`, `binding_sha256`, and
`task_sha256` (row hashes include PostgreSQL `xmin` to detect same-value
rewrites), global FileStorage `upload_count`/`activate_count` call counts,
and the bound archive's `archive_id`, `archive_sha256`, `archive_activated`,
and `zip_files` (`path`, `sha256`, `size`). It returns no file bodies.
The Course journal records method, path, status, actor role, Accept-Language,
multipart media type and presence of a boundary; it excludes credentials.
Root owns the live Next BFF and production rendered Gateway proof, including
canonical preflight, original duplicate-prefix 404, and auth/multipart
negative checks against unchanged bindings and archive call counts.
